page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-288 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 6985P-C processors. It features 288 virtual CPUs mapped across 144 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 1080.0 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows top-tier multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 312,134.69 and a PassMark CPU score of 176,496.48, both placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Memory bandwidth is also highly competitive, reaching 1,062.04 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core CPU performance is moderate, with stress-ng single-core metrics falling into the middle 50%.

The high physical core density and massive 504 MB L3 cache provide strong resource consolidation, offering qualitative cost efficiency for highly parallelized enterprise workloads by reducing the need for multi-node clustering. The server excels in parallelized workloads, demonstrating top-tier results in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and software compilation. While prompt processing for medium (7B) LLM models is in the top 10%, text generation speeds are a notable bottleneck, dropping to the bottom 25% for small models. This profile makes the instance suitable for database operations, parallel build pipelines, and high-throughput web serving.
